partners.mechanism_chain: NOG (HGNC:8044) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (WP:0000001); TGF-beta signaling pathway (WP:0000001) —LEADS_TO→ Multiple synostoses (HP:0002662); SKI (HGNC:10758) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (WP:0000001); TGF-beta signaling pathway (WP:0000001) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000709); TGF-beta signaling pathway (WP:0000001) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal connective tissue (HP:0003204); NOG (HGNC:8044) —LEADS_TO→ Craniosynostosis (HP:0005412); SKI (HGNC:10758) —LEADS_TO→ Craniosynostosis (HP:0005412). Both NOG and SKI act as crucial regulators of the TGF-beta signaling pathway. Haploinsufficiency of NOG in multiple synostoses syndrome 1 leads to dysregulation of this pathway, impacting skeletal development and causing multiple synostoses. Similarly, haploinsufficiency of SKI in Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome also disrupts TGF-beta signaling, contributing to craniosynostosis and skeletal abnormalities. The convergence on the TGF-beta pathway explains the shared phenotypic features, particularly skeletal abnormalities, between these two conditions.
